launches.title: Amazon CloudWatch log centralization now available in AWS GovCloud and additional commercial Regions
launches.excerpt: Amazon CloudWatch log centralization has been launched in the AWS GovCloud (US) partition and thirteen additional commercial Regions worldwide. This feature copies log data from multiple AWS accounts and Regions into a single destination account to streamline monitoring processes. The service integrates directly with AWS Organizations, allowing businesses to aggregate logs efficiently without developing custom solutions. Organisations can apply centralization rules across their entire enterprise, target specific organizational units, or select individual accounts for log aggregation. The system preserves the original source context during the transfer by using enriched system fields. Newly supported locations include Africa (Cape Town), several Asia Pacific hubs, Canada West, multiple European centres, Israel, and the Middle East, alongside both AWS GovCloud (US) regions. Users can initiate the process by establishing a centralization rule through the Amazon CloudWatch console, the AWS CLI, or various AWS SDKs. Customers are permitted to centralize one copy of their logs free of charge, whilst any subsequent copies incur a fee of $0.05 per gigabyte. Further information regarding configuration and a complete list of supported locations can be found in the official Amazon CloudWatch documentation and regional tables.

launches.title: AWS Lambda durable functions are now available in AWS GovCloud (US) Regions
launches.excerpt: Amazon Web Services has announced that Lambda durable functions are now available in both the AWS GovCloud US-West and AWS GovCloud US-East regions. This new feature enables developers to construct reliable multi-step applications and artificial intelligence workflows directly within the standard Lambda developer experience. The functionality extends the existing Lambda programming model by introducing primitives such as step and wait into event handlers. These primitives allow developers to checkpoint progress, recover automatically from failures, and pause executions without incurring compute charges for on-demand functions. By launching in the GovCloud regions, government customers and regulated industries can now orchestrate complex processes like order workflows, user onboarding, and AI-assisted tasks. These implementations can be achieved while simultaneously satisfying stringent security and compliance requirements. Durable functions can be activated for new Lambda functions written in supported languages, including specified versions of Python, Node.js, Go, .Net, and Java. Activation is supported through the AWS Lambda API, the AWS Management Console, and the AWS SDK. Furthermore, developers can utilise infrastructure as code tools such as AWS CloudFormation, AWS Serverless Application Model, and the AWS Cloud Development Kit to manage these deployments. Additional information regarding implementation, regional availability, and associated pricing can be found through official AWS documentation and product pages.

launches.title: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL model now available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
launches.excerpt: Nvidia's Nemotron 3.5 Super VL model has been added to Amazon SageMaker JumpStart, allowing AWS customers to deploy multimodal artificial intelligence solutions. This vision-language model accepts text, images, and video as inputs and generates text outputs. It is built for applications such as document intelligence, graphical user interface understanding, video question answering, and multimodal agentic workflows. The architecture pairs a 120 billion parameter hybrid Mixture-of-Experts language backbone featuring 12 billion active parameters with a vision encoder. The model supports context lengths of up to one million tokens and includes a built-in Multi-Token Prediction head for speculative decoding to accelerate text generation. Reasoning capabilities are configurable per request, and the model supports ten different languages, including English, French, Spanish, German, Japanese, Hindi, Korean, and Chinese. Following multimodal supervised fine-tuning and group relative policy optimisation reinforcement learning, the model provides structured JSON output and tool calling capabilities. SageMaker JumpStart provides two variants for deployment, comprising NVFP4 for optimised inference on G7 instances using Nvidia Blackwell Server Edition graphics processing units, alongside BF16 reference weights for customisation tasks such as domain adaptation, distillation, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning. Customers can deploy the model through the SageMaker JumpStart model catalogue within the SageMaker console or utilise the SageMaker Python SDK to deploy the technology to their AWS accounts.

launches.title: Ubuntu Stonking Stingray swims into spotlight with pre-release kernel
launches.excerpt: Ubuntu 26.10, codenamed Stonking Stingray, has arrived on schedule with the default GNOME 51 edition and a pre-release Linux kernel 7.3. Because Canonical adopted a faster release cycle aligned with AI-boosted kernel updates, the operating system ships with kernel version 7.3 on release candidate seven, with machines set to receive the final version once available. The most noticeable visual update in the GNOME edition is a Windows-like transient pop-up box in the window-tiling assistant that appears when dragging windows to the screen edge. The release also introduces the Myna speech-to-text tool as a technology preview, which requires installing nearly a gigabyte of dependencies and language model files. While the tool struggles with built-in microphones and punctuation commands, performance improves when using a USB headset. All other Ubuntu flavours have also been updated simultaneously, including Kubuntu, Ubuntu MATE, Ubuntu Unity, Ubuntu Budgie, Ubuntu Cinnamon, and Lubuntu, bringing fresh desktop environments and component upgrades. Deeper system changes across all editions include replacing more core command-line tools with Rust versions, swapping dbus-daemon for dbus-broker, and incorporating systemd 261.3. The server variant now includes updates such as AMD ROCm 10.0, OpenSSL 4, and OpenSSH 10.5. Canonical’s TPM-backed full disk encryption is included, though users who enabled it on earlier versions cannot upgrade immediately.

launches.title: Beam model by Reflection is now available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart and AWS Trainium
launches.excerpt: Beam, the inaugural open weight model from US-based company Reflection, has been made available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart within Amazon SageMaker AI. According to the developers, the model delivers strong performance across coding, reasoning, and agentic benchmarks while operating at the frontier of open-source models in its class. Customers can utilise Beam to construct advanced coding agents and automated workflows while maintaining control over their data and infrastructure. The model runs alongside existing models within SageMaker AI and scales to meet production demands using the platform's standard monitoring and audit controls. Furthermore, Beam has been optimised for AWS Trainium, providing users with a cost-efficient deployment option. Engineering teams are able to employ the model for code generation and review, resolving software issues, and automating routine operational tasks. Released under the Apache 2.0 license, the model allows customers to inspect and customise it while keeping their data private within their own AWS accounts. Misha Laskin, co-founder and CEO of Reflection, noted that the integration places frontier AI capabilities directly into the AWS accounts of developers. Accenture Federal Services Chief AI Officer Garrett Berntsen added that the combination of open-weight models and managed infrastructure allows organisations to operate within secure environments. Beam is currently accessible in the US East regions of Northern Virginia and Ohio via Amazon SageMaker JumpStart in Amazon SageMaker Studio.

geo.title: Australian prime minister says lawmaker critically injured by car is 'no accident'
geo.excerpt: An Australian federal independent lawmaker was critically injured on Monday after being struck by a car in what Prime Minister Anthony Albanese described as an apparent deliberate attack. Helen Haines, aged 65, was hit by a Toyota Land Cruiser SUV outside her electoral district office in the Victorian city of Wangaratta. Police stated that a knife was recovered from inside the vehicle following the incident. A 43-year-old man was arrested at the scene by a passerby and will be interviewed by authorities. Prime Minister Albanese confirmed that the national counterterrorism team, which includes police and intelligence agencies, has launched an investigation. Haines was subsequently transported to a hospital with critical injuries. Police noted they are actively investigating whether the collision was an intentional act. The incident has heightened existing safety concerns regarding Australian politicians, who typically operate without security details in a culture of high public accessibility. Official figures show that threats against parliamentarians have doubled over the past three years, with over one thousand threats recorded during the 2025-2026 financial year. Albanese highlighted a growing polarisation in the political climate, noting an increase in shouting and the influence of social media. Similar security concerns have previously arisen in Britain following the murders of lawmakers Jo Cox and David Amess, as well as the recent killing of former politician Ann Widdecombe.

geo.title: 'Lame-duck president' Macron notes 'failures' after France unrest
geo.excerpt: French President Emmanuel Macron has rejected the resignation of Interior Minister Laurent Nunez following a weekend of widespread unrest across the country. The decision was announced on Monday in the wake of severe protests that led to nearly 2,400 arrests. Authorities reported that almost 1,000 police officers and gendarmes sustained injuries during the clashes on Saturday. The violence prompted intense scrutiny of the government's security measures and handling of the demonstrations. Despite the turmoil and calls for accountability within the administration, Macron chose to keep Nunez in his position rather than accept his departure. Further analysis of the situation was provided by France 24 international affairs editor Philip Turle, highlighting the scale of the police casualties and the large number of individuals detained by law enforcement agencies. The events underscore ongoing tensions and public discontent in France, presenting a significant challenge to the government and its security apparatus.

geo.title: World Food Programme to end aid for half a million in Gaza due to funding shortfall
geo.excerpt: The United Nations World Food Programme announced that it will end monthly assistance to 500,000 people in the Gaza Strip due to a funding shortfall. Shaun Hughes, the WFP country director, confirmed that the organisation is cutting half a million people from the total number of individuals it assists. This reduction lowers the number of Palestinians receiving WFP aid, provided as either food or cash assistance, from 1.6 million down to 1.1 million people. Despite the cuts, those still receiving aid represent roughly half of the population in the war-affected territory. The agency issued the warning while noting that overall needs in the region remain acute. The announcement comes at a time when approximately two thirds of the population in the Gaza Strip continues to experience acute food insecurity. Palestinians across the territory have been struggling to find adequate food supplies following prolonged conflict.

geo.title: REPLAY: French PM speaks after crisis meeting
geo.excerpt: French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu announced on Monday that he had asked regional authorities to impose curfews in select cities following a weekend of unrest. The partial and localised measures are specifically intended to safeguard businesses after recent demonstrations spilled over into widespread street violence. During his address following a crisis meeting, Lecornu directed sharp criticism at the ultra-left movement. He accused these groups of deliberately attempting to orchestrate deep unrest throughout the country. According to the Prime Minister, this alleged campaign of disruption is occurring in the critical run-up to next year's presidential election. The government response aims to restore public order and prevent further commercial damage. Authorities are currently coordinating with local officials to implement the requested restrictions in the affected areas. Further details regarding the exact locations and timings of the curfews are expected as regional prefects review the directive.

geo.title: UN food program cuts aid to 500,000 Palestinians in Gaza
geo.excerpt: The United Nations World Food Programme has reduced its monthly food assistance in the Gaza Strip due to severe funding shortages. The agency announced that the number of people receiving aid is being lowered from 1.6 million to 1.1 million, leaving approximately 500,000 individuals without support. Approximately two-thirds of the population in Gaza are currently struggling to access food, with around 1.4 million facing crisis levels of food insecurity and 200,000 living in emergency conditions. Carl Skau, the acting executive director of the WFP, noted that the cuts coincide with the approach of winter, while life remains brutal amid ongoing Israeli strikes, restricted aid, and a lack of proper shelter, basic services, and security despite a ceasefire brokered by the United States last year. The WFP urgently requires $450 million to maintain its critical operations in both Gaza and the West Bank over the upcoming six months. Earlier in September, the agency had already implemented aid reductions in the West Bank because of donor fatigue and financial constraints. Meanwhile, COGAT, the Israeli authority responsible for the Palestinian territories, maintains that the supply of aid deliveries entering the strip exceeds food demand and asserts that there is no acute food insecurity in Gaza.

invest.title: Bank of England said to be reviewing Barclays’ handling of private credit loans
invest.excerpt: The Bank of England’s Prudential Regulation Authority has reportedly begun reviewing Barclays over its handling of loans linked to the private credit sector. The review, initiated earlier this year following concerns raised by a whistleblower, centres on the method Barclays used to log derivatives that finance loans issued to private credit firms. Sources suggest these financial contracts may have been placed in the incorrect portfolio, creating the impression they carried lower risk and potentially allowing the bank to hold insufficient capital while boosting its profitability. Barclays has reportedly accumulated billions of dollars in exposure to private credit loans through these derivatives. In response to the reports, Barclays stated that it takes its regulatory obligations seriously, while the Bank of England declined to comment. Following the news, shares in Barclays dropped by 3.5% on Monday during a wider banking sector sell-off, ahead of the bank’s scheduled financial results. The situation involves the new head of the PRA, Katherine Braddick, who previously worked at Barclays and has been recused from matters concerning the bank until the end of 2026. The scrutiny comes amid broader regulatory anxieties over traditional banks becoming intertwined with the lightly regulated private credit industry, which has recently experienced high-profile company collapses and withdrawal caps. Barclays previously reported financial hits from the failures of automotive companies Tricolor and First Brands, as well as the mortgage lender Market Financial Solutions.
